statement: The function returns a result r and r = the number of integers i such that 1 <= i <= num and ds(i) is even.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000. Let ds(i) denote the sum of the decimal digits of the positive integer i written in base 10 without leading zeros.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds) for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= num.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= 499.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if num = 1.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = floor(num / 2), the number of even positive integers not exceeding num.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 4.
preconditions: num is an I64 and num = 10.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 14.
preconditions: num is an I64 and num = 30.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 249.
preconditions: num is an I64 and num = 500.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 499.
preconditions: num is an I64 and num = 999.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = (the number of integers i with 1 <= i < num and ds(i) even) + (1 if ds(num) is even, otherwise 0).
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000. Let ds(i) denote the sum of the decimal digits of the positive integer i.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 1 <= k < num, the number of integers i with 1 <= i <= k and ds(i) even is at most r.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 1 <= num <= 1000. Let ds(i) denote the sum of the decimal digits of the positive integer i.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 1 and the integer 2, whose digit sum is 2 and hence even, is one of the integers counted in the main specification.
preconditions: num is an I64 whose mathematical value satisfies 2 <= num <= 1000.
